title: k-fold Chinese Remainder Theorem: ℤ/(n₁···nₖ)ℤ ≅ ∏ᵢ ℤ/nᵢℤ
description: The Chinese Remainder Theorem extends from two coprime moduli to any finite list of pairwise coprime moduli. For pairwise coprime n₁, ..., nₖ, the ring ℤ/(n₁···nₖ)ℤ is isomorphic to the product ∏ᵢ ℤ/nᵢℤ. This formalization constructs the k-fold isomorphism by induction using Mathlib's 2-fold ZMod.chineseRemainder, with the key lemma that pairwise coprimality implies coprimality with the product of remaining moduli. Includes explicit 3-fold and 4-fold specializations and k-fold Euler totient multiplicativity.

CRTProd: Right-associated product type CRTProd (n :: ns) = ZMod n × CRTProd ns
coprime_prod_of_coprime_all: n coprime to each nᵢ implies n coprime to ∏ nᵢ

overview.historicalContext: The Chinese Remainder Theorem has ancient roots (Sunzi Suanjing, ~3rd century) and was generalized by Euler and Gauss. The 2-fold case (m coprime to n implies unique solution mod mn) extends to k-fold: for pairwise coprime n₁, ..., nₖ, the system x ≡ aᵢ (mod nᵢ) has a unique solution mod n₁···nₖ. The ring-theoretic formulation as an isomorphism ℤ/(∏nᵢ)ℤ ≅ ∏ᵢ ℤ/nᵢℤ captures both existence and uniqueness, plus the multiplicative structure.
overview.problemStatement:
**Theorem (crtKFold)**: For a list ns of pairwise coprime natural numbers,
  ZMod ns.prod ≃+* CRTProd ns
where CRTProd ns is the right-associated product ∏ᵢ ZMod (ns.get i).

**Key lemma (coprime_prod_of_coprime_all)**: If n is coprime to every element of ns, then n is coprime to ns.prod.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Induction on the list of moduli**:

**Base**: Empty list — ZMod 1 ≅ PUnit (the trivial ring).

**Step**: Given n :: ns with pairwise coprimality:
1. By coprime_prod_of_coprime_all, n is coprime to ns.prod
2. Apply ZMod.chineseRemainder: ZMod (n * ns.prod) ≅ ZMod n × ZMod ns.prod
3. Apply IH: ZMod ns.prod ≅ CRTProd ns
4. Compose via RingEquiv.prodCongr

**Explicit specializations**: crt3 and crt4 construct 3-fold and 4-fold CRTs directly using associativity and mul_right, avoiding the CRTProd type.
keyInsights: The key enabling lemma is coprime_prod_of_coprime_all: pairwise coprimality propagates to products
CRTProd as a recursive type avoids the ZMod (n*1) ≠ ZMod n definitional equality issue
The base case ZMod 1 ≅ PUnit uses Subsingleton since ZMod 1 has exactly one element
Explicit crt3/crt4 use ring to prove associativity a*b*c = a*(b*c) at the ℕ level
All coprimality conditions are decidable, so examples use `by decide`

sections.title: Key Coprimality Lemma
sections.summary: coprime_prod_of_coprime_all and head_coprime_tail_prod: if n is coprime to each element, it's coprime to the product. Proved by induction using Nat.Coprime.mul_right.

sections.title: Explicit 3-fold and 4-fold CRT
sections.summary: crt3 and crt4: direct constructions of ℤ/(abc)ℤ ≅ ℤ/aℤ × ℤ/bℤ × ℤ/cℤ and 4-fold analog. Uses ring for ℕ associativity and Nat.Coprime.mul_right for coprimality.

sections.title: General k-fold CRT Isomorphism
sections.summary: CRTProd recursive type and crtKFold: the main inductive construction. Base case via zmod_one_equiv_punit, step via chineseRemainder + prodCongr.

sections.title: Properties and Totient Multiplicativity
sections.summary: Bijection, injectivity, surjectivity, ring hom properties, round-trips. Plus totient_prod_pairwise_coprime: φ(∏nᵢ) = ∏φ(nᵢ).

sections.title: Concrete Examples
sections.summary: Concrete instances: ℤ/30ℤ ≅ ℤ/2ℤ × ℤ/3ℤ × ℤ/5ℤ and ℤ/210ℤ ≅ ℤ/2ℤ × ℤ/3ℤ × ℤ/5ℤ × ℤ/7ℤ. Totient example: φ(30) = φ(2)·φ(3)·φ(5).

conclusion.summary: This formalization proves the k-fold Chinese Remainder Theorem with 0 axioms and 0 sorries: ZMod (∏ nᵢ) ≅ ∏ᵢ ZMod nᵢ for pairwise coprime nᵢ. The proof constructs the isomorphism by induction using Mathlib's 2-fold chineseRemainder, with explicit specializations for 3 and 4 moduli. The k-fold Euler totient multiplicativity follows as a corollary.
conclusion.implications:
**For number theory**: The k-fold CRT provides the foundation for prime factorization-based decompositions, Hensel lifting, and number-theoretic algorithms.

**For algebra**: Demonstrates the pattern of building k-ary constructions from binary ones using induction on lists.

**For Mathlib**: Could be contributed as a generalization of the existing ZMod.chineseRemainder.
openQuestions: Generalize to the ideal-theoretic CRT: R/∏Iᵢ ≅ ∏ R/Iᵢ for pairwise coprime ideals
Prove cardinality preservation: |ZMod (∏nᵢ)| = ∏|ZMod nᵢ| = ∏nᵢ for the k-fold case
Connect to the Pi-type formulation: ZMod (∏ nᵢ) ≅ (i : Fin k) → ZMod (ns i)
